narrative_purpose: Makes the central idea visible before the math: two population waves that rise and fall together but out of step, the predator wave cresting after the prey wave, so the reader feels the lag the Lotka-Volterra model predicts.
subject: Two smooth glowing wave-trails flowing across a deep indigo atmospheric field, aligned along a shared horizontal baseline: an upper cyan wave representing herbivore abundance, and a lower magenta wave representing predator abundance. The crests of the magenta wave are consistently shifted to the right of the cyan peaks, depicting the predator's delayed response to prey abundance. Minimal glowing silhouettes of a six-legged browser and a sleek pack hunter ride their respective crests in glowing starlight.
scene: An abstract naturalist field plate showing two coupled luminous wave trajectories against deep indigo space, illustrating the cyclic phase lag between prey and predator populations.
camera: Flat head-on naturalist cutaway view of the two stacked waves.
light: Self-luminous curves and silhouettes against dark; no external light source.
palette: Void-indigo ground, living-teal for the prey wave, biolum-magenta for the predator wave, no other accent.
style: Painterly plate that reads as a diagram through composition alone, soft glowing wave-trails, not a hard vector chart.
detail_level: Moderate: curves clean and legible, the rightward shift of the magenta crests obvious, silhouettes simple.
composition: Two horizontal wave streams spanning the frame against deep indigo darkness, leaving generous negative space above and below.
consistency_notes: Teal = prey, magenta = predator, the same colour coding used by the chapter's interactive oscillator. Reads as a teaching picture.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no numbers, no labels, no tick marks, no arrows, no grid, no diagram chrome, no photographic or 3D-render look
